caption.verbatim: Figure 1: Bathtub Geometry

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 1: Bathtub Geometry

mention.lead_sentence: The bathtub will be considered as a rectangular prism, with dimensions equal to L, W , and H as shown below in Figure 1.

items.note: The tub drawn as a shaded three-dimensional box in perspective with the water surface shaded, a drain hole at the lower right, a faucet pipe entering at the upper left and the three edge lengths lettered H, W and L on dimension arrows. No axis graduations, no legend, no scale, no printed number: the L, W and H it letters are the symbols the prose then carries into the model, not measured values. It is the geometric premise of the whole paper and the only exhibit that shows the tub itself.

caption.verbatim: Figure 2: Cross-sectional Fluid Element

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 2: Cross-sectional Fluid Element
items.note: A cross-section of the water drawn as a shaded rectangle with a double-line boundary, dimension arrows for H, W and delta-x and a small x-y-z axis triad. The caption calls it the cross-sectional fluid element, but the drawing carries NO velocity arrow and NO force arrow: it fixes the dimensions of the element, and the prose that follows it does the rest. No legend, no graduation, no number. Note that the caption is the only thing in the paper that names this drawing - the surrounding sentence ('Heat capacity, fluid flow velocity, heat loss to the surroundings, and other extensive properties') runs straight through it in the text layer, which is why the line reads 'Heat capacity, Figure 2: Cross-sectional Fluid Element'.

caption.verbatim: Figure 3: Linear Enthalpy Variation

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 3: Linear Enthalpy Variation

mention.lead_sentence: as- sumption was validated using property val- ues from the XSteam[1] MATLAB function, shown at right in Figure 3.

items.note: One straight blue line across a light grid, with a short black arrow pointing at the fitted equation printed on the plot ('h = 4.1854u + 0.21431'). Axes: temperature on the abscissa 0 to 100 deg C, specific enthalpy on the ordinate 0 to 450 kJ/kg. No legend, no marker, no printed data value; the only number in the picture besides the tick labels is the slope the caption's 'linear' refers to. It is the paper's evidence for assuming constant specific heat and it fits in one straight line, so the exhibit and the claim agree.

Axes: water temperature 30 to 50 deg C, heat transfer coefficient 0 to 5.5 W/m2K. No printed data values beyond the mean in the key. items.note: The final state of the whole paper: a blocky field, dark blue at the margins and a yellow band across the interior, colour bar at the right spanning 30 to 37 deg C, in-plot title 'Optimized PID Heat Map'. note:
Paper 92, Team 44845, the hot-bath thermal-fluid paper. Forty-four pages, fifty-three measured
regions over twenty-nine of them, and the fifty-three resolve into FIFTY FIGURE ROWS, ONE TABLE and
TWO EXCLUSIONS. Unaccounted zero. The paper prints thirty-five figure captions and NO table caption
or table number in any of its forty-four pages: the single table is the unlabelled parameter grid on
p11, named only by the p10 sentence "The following table contains the model parameters that can be
altered as well as their nominal values". Fifteen exhibits are two-panel and supply thirty of the
fifty rows; the panels are boxed separately and each row keeps its own family, so Figure 18, Figure
32 and Figure 33 each contribute one heat map row and one line-plot row under a single caption.

Citation is uneven. Fourteen of the thirty-five captions are carried into a pointer sentence - "as
shown below in Figure 1", "shown at right in Figure 3", "this is shown in Figure 7 at right",
"Figure 11 displays", "shown in Figure 22 below" - and twenty-one figures are named by no sentence
at all, most of them in the sensitivity sections where the pointer degenerates into "shown below" or
"a similar plot is shown below" with no label. Four pointers sit a page before their figure: Figures 24, 31,
32 and 35 are each introduced on the page before the one that prints them. The worst case
is Figure 33: p38 writes "The same results are shown in 33 below", dropping the word "Figure"
entirely, so no page of the paper ever prints "Figure 33".

Two captions could not be quoted from the linear text layer at all, because the two-column wrap runs
the caption's second line through the body column: p11 gives "Figure 7: Graphical Illustration of the
Ther- be zero, as no mass or energy can be accu- modynamic System" and p35 gives "Figure 29:
Illustration of Properly Tuned of the three components of a PID controller PID Controller[11]". Both
are typed from the printed block geometry, hyphen break included. Figure 29 also carries a label from
its source: the raster itself prints "Figure 20a. Illustration of Properly Tuned", so a foreign
figure number is baked into the paper's own Figure 29, and its abscissa is labelled with a bare "t"
and its ordinate not at all. Figure 16's in-plot title misspells "propagation" as "Propogation";
Figure 23's panel title reads "Varied of Diffusivity over Full Length"; Figure 28's first panel title
is clipped mid-phrase.

The exhibits themselves are honest about one thing and careless about another. Honest: the three
heat-transfer-coefficient plots (Figures 4, 5, 6) each print the mean they are replaced by, and the
two near-flat body-property panels (Figure 28) visibly justify that substitution. Careless: almost
every comparison pair is drawn on non-common scales. Figures 19(a) and 19(b), 20(a) and 20(b), 21(a)
and 21(b), 25(a) and 25(b) and 26(a) and 26(b) use colour or ordinate windows that differ by an order
of magnitude, so the "comparison" cannot be read off the page without rescaling one half; Figure 10
fills its frame with a slope whose ordinate spans 1.8 deg C; Figure 22 puts the same objective
function on two ordinates at once; Figures 32(b) and 33(b) certify uniformity with colour bars 0.0003
deg C wide. No exhibit in the paper prints a raw data value on its marks except the three annotated
optima (38.0425 deg C, 0.006518 kg/s) and the borrowed gains Kp = 5, Ki = 3, Kd = 3 of Figure 29.

Families: line 31, heatmap-or-contour 16, flowchart-or-schematic 3, table-grid 1. The two excluded
regions are form lettering (p1's control box) and logo art (p44's consulting-firm letterhead).
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: fifty-three measured regions resolve into fifty figure rows, one table and two exclusions, and no region is counted twice [place.page_order].

A panel measured as its own box is its own row: the fifteen two-panel exhibits of this paper (Figures 17 to 28, 32, 33 and 34) are split into two measured boxes each, so the figure count follows the boxes and panel_count names the exhibit the row belongs to [geometry.panel_count].

A panel's family is its own, not its exhibit's: Figure 18 pairs a heat map with a line plot and Figures 32 and 33 pair a line plot with a heat map, so the two rows of one captioned exhibit can carry different families [geometry.family].

Two ordinates carrying the SAME quantity are a geometry defect, not a family: Figures 22, 30, 31 and 34 print left and right y axes both labelled or both serving the same objective function, and the rows stay line rather than composite [geometry.family].

A table with no caption and no printed label is still a table: the p11 grid is named only by the p10 pointer sentence 'The following table contains the model parameters', so its caption_source is none and its numbering is none [place.section_kind].

A caption the linear text layer cannot carry is typed from the printed block geometry: the two-column wrap interleaves Figures 7 and 29 with the body text, so both are transcribed from the block as printed rather than quoted from the page string [place.doc_order].

Form lettering and logo art boxed as regions are not exhibits: the summary-sheet control box on p1 and the consulting-firm letterhead on p44 are excluded as not-an-exhibit rather than counted as figures [place.area_frac].

Section placement follows the printed heading positions: a region on p7 above the 3.2 heading belongs to 3.1 and a region on p35 above the 9.2 heading belongs to 9.1, whatever carry-over the context dump reports [place.section_path].

mention.lead_sentence: The following table contains the model parameters that can be altered as well as their nominal values.

tables.note: The paper's only table and it is UNLABELLED: three columns (Parameter, Description, Nominal Value) with vertical strokes between the columns and a single horizontal rule under the header row, twenty rows in all - the header plus nineteen parameters (L, W, H, bath volume, water density, specific heat, thermal conductivity, three heat transfer coefficients, ambient temperature, inlet temperature, mass flow, body dimensions and body properties). Units sit inside the cells of the third column rather than in the header, bracketed citation superscripts ([2], [3]) sit inside cells too, and no cell is shaded. The paper never prints 'Table 1': the grid is named only by the p10 pointer sentence, and because the pointer calls it 'the following table' the caption block is empty rather than absent.
